subject: Clarify penetration test coverage across Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC / on-prem) - Stellardata request
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jmiles@stellardata.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@stellardata.com, Kavita Patel <kpatel@stellardata.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pen test coverage question: which Redwood environments are in-scope?

Hi Vanessa,

Stellardata's security team is preparing our vendor assessment and we need a quick clarification on the scope of Redwood's most recent penetration test. Specifically: which deployment modes were included in the scope of the pen test you can share (Hosted API, Dedicated pools, Private/VPC deployments, on-prem agent installs)? We also want to confirm whether Dedicated instances that are deployed into a customer's VPC (but managed by Redwood) are considered in-scope.

If you can point us to the pen test report and a short scope matrix, that would be ideal — even a one-pager that says what Redwood is responsible for vs what the customer is responsible for.

Thanks,
Jordan Miles
Head of SecOps — Stellardata
security@stellardata.com

P.S. We have a compliance questionnaire due next week (SIG/CAIQ). Any quick notes you can include about residual risk items would help us sign off faster.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <jmiles@stellardata.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-04T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test coverage question: which Redwood environments are in-scope?

Thanks Jordan — looping in our security and infra leads for the exact boundaries and any artifacts we can share. Quick answers up front: Hosted API and Redwood-managed Dedicated pools are fully in-scope for our internal pen tests. Private/VPC and on-prem packages are nuanced — parts that we manage are in-scope, but customer-owned networks and hardware are out-of-scope unless there's an explicit engagement where the customer provides test access.

Laura / Rishi — can you confirm the latest report/attachments we can share with Stellardata and whether the Dedicated-in-customer-VPC case needs extra paperwork? Jordan — we'll try to attach the latest report and a short matrix in the next message. If helpful, I'm available for a 30-min sync — propose Wed 10/6 10am PT.

- Vanessa
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <jmiles@stellardata.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-04T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test coverage question: which Redwood environments are in-scope?

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear question. Apologies for the long-ish reply but the boundaries matter, so I want to be precise. Below is a short scope matrix and the current remediation status for our most recent internal engagement (report attached).

Scope summary (high-level):
- Hosted API (redwood-managed control plane & compute): fully in scope. This includes API endpoints, control plane services, model-serving runtime in our managed accounts, and the telemetry pipelines we operate.
- Redwood Dedicated (Redwood-managed, reserved GPU pools in our cloud accounts): in scope. These are dedicated infra pools owned and operated by Redwood — pen test covers OS, hypervisor/config, network controls, and our runtime.
- Dedicated deployed into a customer's cloud account / customer VPC: partially in scope. If the instance is provisioned and operated by Redwood (we manage the VM and runtime) but sits in a customer VPC, we only test the Redwood-managed components. Customer-owned network configuration, private subnets, and cross-account routing are the customer's responsibility and out-of-scope unless the customer signs an authorization and provides test access.
- Private (VPC/private control plane) and on-prem: mixed. For our Private VPC offering (Redwood control plane connecting to customer-hosted model runners), we test the Redwood components we ship/operate (agents, control-plane connectors). Any infrastructure fully owned and operated by the customer (on-prem hardware, local network, customer-managed KMS) is out-of-scope.

Attachments included for Stellardata:
- redwood-pt-202608-report.pdf (redacted internal test report, Aug 2026)
- scope-matrix-pt.xlsx (one-page scope matrix you can include in your assessment)

Remediation status (from last report):
- MEDIUM: insecure TLS config on legacy admin endpoint — RESOLVED (patched 2026-09-15).
- MEDIUM: insufficient session timeout on internal admin console — RESOLVED (config change 2026-09-20).
- LOW: verbose debug logging in a background job that could leak internal paths — MITIGATED, final validation in progress. Expected close by 2026-10-08.

If Stellardata needs a statement of scope or a signed penetration test attestation, we can produce a scoped addendum that describes responsibilities and an agreed test window. For Dedicated-in-customer-VPC scenarios we generally require a short addendum and temporary test-accounts or IP allowlist.

Let me know what level of evidence you need (full report vs redacted vs SOC 2 controls mapping).

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Information Security — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

[Attachment: redwood-pt-202608-report.pdf]
[Attachment: scope-matrix-pt.xlsx]

From: Jordan Miles <jmiles@stellardata.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test coverage question: which Redwood environments are in-scope?

Laura — thanks, that's really helpful. One follow-up: our procurement team is evaluating a Dedicated deployment where Redwood will manage the instance but it will live in our VPC (we want traffic to remain in our account). From your note, it sounds like we should expect the test to cover the Redwood-managed runtime only and not our networking. We will probably need a short addendum and a contact to coordinate IP allowlists.

Can we get a one-paragraph statement that I can attach to our SIG/CAIQ response (something like: "Redwood's penetration testing covers Redwood-managed compute and control plane components; customer-managed network and hardware are excluded unless explicitly agreed in writing"). If you can send that short clause and confirm who on your side will coordinate the addendum, we can move quickly.

Thanks, Jordan

On Wed, Oct 4, 2026 at 11:02 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <jmiles@stellardata.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-06T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test coverage question: which Redwood environments are in-scope?

Jordan / team — quick operational clarification from infra: your summary is correct. To be explicit for procurement language, you can use this clause: 

"Redwood Inference conducts penetration testing against Redwood-managed components only. For Dedicated deployments, Redwood-managed compute and runtime instances (even when provisioned within a customer's cloud account) are in scope only for the software and configuration under Redwood's operational control. Customer-owned network configurations, private subnets, on-premise hardware, and customer-managed key material are out-of-scope unless otherwise agreed in a written authorization and test plan."
If Stellardata wants Redwood to include customer-network-level testing (e.g., routing rules, private load balancers), we will require an explicit scope addendum and temporary test credentials or a jump-host / bastion provided by the customer. We've attached a short boundary doc (dedicated-vpc-boundary.docx) that procurement/security can use as the starting point for an addendum. Once you confirm, we can draft the addendum and propose a test window.

Current remediation note: the final validation on the low finding completed today in our QA environment; we'll publish the closure ticket tomorrow and attach the remediation-plan-202610.pdf.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Infrastructure Security — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
